standard_prerequisites.name: Monotone enumerations of maximal universal trees
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every Sigma^0_1 formula and every condition there is a monotone enumeration of a maximal universal tree satisfying the formula, and the tree is a set of nodes closed downward under prefixes with the universality property of the SEM section; the author's own statement is retained at source lines 863-865 and the definitions of trees at 853-861.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof builds the enumeration for the specific formula that codes an initial segment of the jump, so both the existence statement and the notion of tree must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite maximal universal tree forces a last true instance
standard_prerequisites.statement: If the enumeration is M-finite, then there is an extension of the condition and an index q such that the extension forces the formula at the index below q and forces its negation at q; retained with this card at source lines 893-897.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies this lemma to the enumeration once the enumeration is known to be M-finite, which is what turns the tree statement into the forcing statement about the jump.

standard_prerequisites.name: The theory BME_* and the bound k on the enumerated formula
standard_prerequisites.statement: Since the ordinal is positive the model satisfies WF(omega^omega) and therefore the principle BME_* of bounded monotone enumerations, which is what makes the enumeration M-finite; moreover the specific formula is built so that it never holds at the index k+1, which bounds the enumeration.
standard_prerequisites.use: These two facts supply the M-finiteness hypothesis and the finiteness of the tree that the proof needs before it can invoke the finite-tree lemma.

core_obligations: Define the Sigma^0_1(Y) formula that holds when there are indices e_0 below ... below e_{x-1} below k such that the functional with each index converges at that index on the generic (source line 922).
Invoke the maximal enumeration lemma to obtain a monotone enumeration of a maximal universal tree satisfying that formula (source line 924).
Observe that the enumeration is bounded by k because the formula fails at the index k+1, since the required increasing sequence of indices cannot then be found below k (source line 925).
Use that the model satisfies WF(omega^omega), hence the principle of bounded monotone enumerations, to conclude that the bounded enumeration is M-finite (source line 926).

Apply the finite-tree forcing lemma to that M-finite maximal universal tree to obtain an extension and an index q such that the extension forces the formula at q minus one and forces its negation at q (source line 927).

Read off the initial segment of the jump: let sigma' be the set of indices below k at which the functional converges on the extension, and conclude that the extension forces the k-th initial segment of the jump of G plus Y to equal sigma' (source line 928).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the formula coding the jump segment and take a maximal universal enumeration for it.
Bound the enumeration by k and use bounded monotone enumeration to get M-finiteness.
Apply the finite-tree lemma and read off the forced initial segment of the jump.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sem-wf-forcing-jump（源 918-920 行，证明 921-929 行）：SEM 力迫中任一条件都有扩展把一个 M-有限串 σ' 强制为 (G⊕Y)' 的前 k 位。关键操作不是例行核验：作者先把「跳跃初段」编码成一个 Σ⁰₁(Y) 公式（922 行），取它的极大泛树枚举（924 行），再说明该枚举 k-有界（因为公式在指标 k+1 处恒假，925 行），并由 M ⊨ WF(ω^ω) 推出 M ⊨ BME_* 从而枚举 M-有限（926 行）——这一步是把「树」转成可套用有限树引理的关键；最后用有限树引理得到强制 φ(G,q−1) 与 ¬φ(G,q) 的扩展，并读出 σ' 完成论证（927-928 行）。难点在于跨越「有界枚举」到「M-有限」以及把公式的真假位与跳跃的位对齐；原文位置在证明的 922-928 行。
